input.question: How did the advancement of using fossils help geological science in the early 20th century?
input.context: At the beginning of the 20th century, important advancement in geological science was facilitated by the ability to obtain accurate absolute dates to geologic events using radioactive isotopes and other methods. This changed the understanding of geologic time. Previously, geologists could only use fossils and stratigraphic correlation to date sections of rock relative to one another. With isotopic dates it became possible to assign absolute ages to rock units, and these absolute dates could be applied to fossil sequences in which there was datable material, converting the old relative ages into new absolute ages.

Context:
At the beginning of the 20th century, important advancement in geological science was facilitated by the ability to obtain accurate absolute dates to geologic events using radioactive isotopes and other methods. This changed the understanding of geologic time. Previously, geologists could only use fossils and stratigraphic correlation to date sections of rock relative to one another. With isotopic dates it became possible to assign absolute ages to rock units, and these absolute dates could be applied to fossil sequences in which there was datable material, converting the old relative ages into new absolute ages.

Question:
How did the advancement of using fossils help geological science in the early 20th century?

Answer:

response.prediction: The advancement of using fossils, combined with the new ability to obtain accurate absolute dates through radioactive isotopes, allowed geologists to convert previously relative ages of rock layers and fossils into absolute ages. Before this, geologists could only determine the sequence and relative ages of rock units and fossils using stratigraphy and fossil correlation. With isotopic dating, geologists could assign specific numerical ages to rocks that contained datable material, and by linking these dated rocks to fossil-bearing layers, they could now determine the actual ages of those fossils and the geologic events they represented. This greatly improved the precision and understanding of Earth's history.
